title: Tom Cruise Is Confident Paramount-Warner Bros. Will Release 30 Films a Year After Merger: ‘They’re Going to Deliver’
description:
Sep 1, 2026 3:07pm PT	
	

	
		Tom Cruise Is Confident Paramount-Warner Bros. Will Release 30 Films a Year After Merger: ‘They’re Going
body:
Sep 1, 2026 3:07pm PT	
	

	
		Tom Cruise Is Confident Paramount-Warner Bros. Will Release 30 Films a Year After Merger: ‘They’re Going to Deliver’
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Getty Images for CinemaCon
	

		
	
				
	Tom Cruise is confident David Ellison will deliver on his promise of 30 films a year from a combined Paramount and Warner Bros.

	“I think it’s awesome,” Cruise told “The Pat McAfee Show.” “You know, here’s the thing. They’re going to deliver 30 movies. It’s a community to me. It’s not an industry. The people in these studios are not just people in the studios. They’re my family. I know we’re going to get those 30 movies. I want us all to come together as a community to help make those 30 movies. It’s not just going to be, you know, Paramount doing it. Everyone’s going to need all the help of every artist to be able to do it.” 
	

	Cruise has long made a home at Paramount, which released all eight films in his marquee “Mission: Impossible” franchise, starting with the 1996 original. His other collaborations with Paramount include the “Top Gun” movies, “The Firm,” “Vanilla Sky,” “Collateral,” “War of the Worlds,” “Jack Reacher,” and “Days of Thunder,” which is getting a sequel in 2028. Cruise, never shy about the affiliation, went as far as climbing the Paramount water tower for the studio’s CinemaCon 2025 presentation featurette. 


	More to come…


	
		More from Variety

schema.headline: Tom Cruise Is Confident Paramount-Warner Bros. Will Release 30 Films a Year After Merger: ‘They’re Going to Deliver’

title: Melissa Leo Joins Will Smith in Amazon MGM and Miramax Action-Thriller ‘Supermax’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Oscar and Emmy winner Melissa Leo has joined the cast of Amazon MGM Studios and Miramax’s action-thriller “Supermax,” starring Will Smith.

	David G
body:
Oscar and Emmy winner Melissa Leo has joined the cast of Amazon MGM Studios and Miramax’s action-thriller “Supermax,” starring Will Smith.

	David Gordon Green directs the film, which follows two FBI agents investigating a seemingly impossible murder within the impenetrable walls of a maximum-security prison. Lee — whose role remains under wraps — joins the previously announced ensemble cast led by Smith, AnnaSophia Robb, Jason Clarke, and Jaafar Jackson. The movie also features Nicholas Alexander Chavez, Andrés Almeida, Martin Bats Bradford, and Erika Ringor. 
	

	“Supermax” is currently in production in New South Wales, Australia, with Gordon Green (“Halloween”) directing from a script by David Weil and David J. Rosen (“Hunters,” “Invasion”). In May, Amazon MGM acquired the worldwide rights to the movie from Miramax for $70 million, with the film slated for release on Prime Video.


	The Picture Company’s Andrew Rona and Alex Heineman are producing the film with Smith and Adam Fishbach for Smith’s company Westbrook Studios. Weil and Rosen will also serve as executive producers alongside Miramax CEO Jonathan Glickman, president of film Alexandra Loewy, COO Thom Zadra, and senior VP Spencer Ela. James Lassiter and Miguel Melendez will also executive produce for Westbrook Studios. Westbrook’s Symone Crews serves as associate producer alongside Natalie Laine Williams.

	Leo’s acclaimed filmography is highlighted by her Oscar-winning performance in David O. Russell’s “The Fighter,” plus a nomination for “Frozen River.” On TV, Leo won an Emmy for her work on FX’s “Louie.” She was previously nominated for HBO’s “Mildred Pierce” and “All The Way.” Leo’s resume also includes “King Ivory,” “The Knife,” “Prisoners,” “The Equalizer,” “Novitiate,” “I Know This Much Is True” and “I’m Dying Up Here.”
	

	Leo most recently starred in Paramount’s supernatural horror film “Passenger,” which is now streaming on Paramount+, and she just wrapped a lead role opposite Lili Reinhart in Sean Byrne’s “The Mannequin” for Studiocanal. Leo will also appear in Josh Penn Soskin’s “The Rooster Prince,” opposite Shia LaBeouf and Jackson White. She is represented by Gersh.

schema.headline: Melissa Leo Joins Will Smith in Amazon MGM and Miramax Action-Thriller ‘Supermax’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Ariana Grande Tears Up as She Ends ‘Eternal Sunshine’ Tour Ahead of Step Back From Visibility: ‘I Have Loved Every Minute of This’
description: Ariana Grande took a moment during the final show of her “Eternal Sunshine” tour to thank the audience at London’s O2 Arena, sharing how it’s been a
body:
Ariana Grande took a moment during the final show of her “Eternal Sunshine” tour to thank the audience at London’s O2 Arena, sharing how it’s been an “extraordinary experience” across her 41 shows.

	“I just want to say thank you so much,” said Grande, seated on a stool on the B-stage. “This has been such an extraordinary experience. Thank you for 10 beautiful London shows and for 41 incredible Eternal Sunshine tour shows.


	“This has been one of the most beautiful, extraordinary experiences of my life and I just want to express my gratitude without sobbing completely,” she continued, choking back tears. “But really, thank you from the bottom of my heart, it’s been so special and I’ll cherish this experience always and I have the best fans in the entire world and I always have. And I love your outfits, I love your faces, I love seeing you, I love connecting with you in this way. Thank you for all of your effort for making this so special. All your messages and your costumes and your wardrobe and makeup is just so beautiful. I have loved every minute of this with you all and I just want to make sure I express how grateful I am. Thank you and I love you so much.”
	


	Grande kicked off her “Eternal Sunshine” tour in June with a trio of shows at Oakland Arena in California. Throughout the North American trek, she performed a handful of shows in various markets including Los Angeles, Austin, Atlanta, New York City, Boston, Montreal and Chicago. In mid-August, she traveled across the Pond for 10 shows at London’s O2 Arena, where she brought the journey to a close on Tuesday evening.
	

	During the tour, Grande declared that she would be stepping out of the spotlight for an extended break following its conclusion. In early August, a rep for Grande cited “ongoing public scrutiny” as one of the reasons for the pause, and said that she “looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both happily and healthily.” In tandem, Grande bowed out of Stephen Sondheim’s West End revival of “Sunday in the Park With George.”

	Grande later clarified that the break, which was announced amid speculation about her well-being and health, was planned in advance and was not a “reactive or impulsive thing.” “It is something that I had decided to plan that I had quietly made a long time ago and it’s a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place,” she told the crowd in Chicago in early August. “And I want you to know many things can be true at the same time. I want to share this because I heard that my fans were worried that negativity was ruining things for me, but I just have to say that could not be more the fuck opposite. Honestly, this is not what that is.”

schema.headline: Ariana Grande Tears Up as She Ends ‘Eternal Sunshine’ Tour Ahead of Step Back From Visibility: ‘I Have Loved Every Minute of This’

title: Jason Isbell Leads New Suno Lawsuit, Claims AI Music Generator ‘Exploits’ Musicians’ Identities in Models
description: Grammy-winning Americana crooner Jason Isbell is one of several new litigants in a new federal lawsuit against the AI music generator Suno, arguing
body:
Grammy-winning Americana crooner Jason Isbell is one of several new litigants in a new federal lawsuit against the AI music generator Suno, arguing the company has allowed users to produce tracks based on musicians’ identities with its models without their consent.

	The lawsuit — filed Monday in the U.S. District Court in Massachusetts by a group that includes Isbell, Cracker and Camper Van Beethoven frontman David Lowery, Texas blues musician Guy Forsyth and Florida-based saxophonist Eduardo Calle — compared Suno to the Borg, the “Star Trek” villains known for their “resistance is futile” method of absorbing their victims into their hive mind by restructuring their minds to become a similar, if changed versions of themselves. That is what Suno does when users type an artist’s name into its models to try and produce sonic variants of their work, attorney Alan D. Rose wrote in the complaint for the plaintiffs. 
	

	“It encoded musicians’ identities into its AI model to create its commercial product without consent, and now exploits those identities by publicly using musicians’ names to Suno’s considerable commercial benefit,” Rose wrote, claiming the company encouraged its marketing partners to tout that ability while minimizing the company’s alleged choice. 


	The plaintiffs are seeking class-action status for the lawsuit, statutory and punitive damages and for Suno to be prevented from capturing and monetizing artists’ identities. “A musician’s identity is their property, but Suno took it without consent,” Rose wrote. “This lawsuit is how these musicians resist the premise that resistance is futile.”
	

	Suno declined to comment. The company’s CEO Mikey Shulman wrote in a blog post last month that Suno did not retain artist names in its metadata and that its models did not allow users to prompt for specific artists or songs.

	But the plaintiffs claimed that Suno retained “voiceprints” of artists, and users could bypass Suno’s guardrails and access those “prints” by specific prompts that skirt using the artist’s name by asking for tracks invoking their “tone and phrasing,” by using real names instead of stage names (as in the case of the rapper Common) or by adding spaces between the letters of their names, among other methods.

	The case differs from other litigation efforts against Suno for focusing not on the issues of copyright, which have spurred several lawsuits against the company and thus settlements providing certain catalogues for Suno’s use, and instead on the element of identity, which the plaintiffs claimed is usually retained by a musician regardless of a settlement deal or whether an artist opts into allowing Suno to train off their work.

	“Many musicians sell their rights to specific recordings,” the complaint read. “However, the identity right belongs to the performer regardless of who owns any copyright in an underlying recording unless the identity right is separately licensed, typically for merchandise under an artist’s control. This lawsuit seeks to recover the value of those misappropriated identities and to stop their ongoing commercial exploitation.”

	Other lawsuits against Suno include ongoing cases by the independent music publisher Round Hill Music and the major labels Universal Music Group and Sony Music Entertainment. Warner Music Group settled its case against Suno last year, and Suno is developing a model in partnership with the label.

schema.headline: Jason Isbell Leads New Suno Lawsuit, Claims AI Music Generator ‘Exploits’ Musicians’ Identities in Models

title: ‘VIII: Awakening’ Wraps Production in Beijing, Marking KC Global Media Asia’s First China Original (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Production has wrapped in Beijing on “VIII: Awakening,” KC Global Media Asia’s fantasy adventure drama reimagining a classic Chinese mythology legen
body:
Production has wrapped in Beijing on “VIII: Awakening,” KC Global Media Asia’s fantasy adventure drama reimagining a classic Chinese mythology legend for modern audiences. 

	The S-grade series, the company’s first original China production, completed 24 15-minute episodes for its debut season.

	The story follows insurance investigator Lu Xian, who awakens a mysterious precognitive power and discovers he is descended from an ancient legendary guardian. He must join forces with seven others to thwart a dangerous plot as an imprisoned clan of dragons threatens its return. The group uncovers betrayal within its own ranks and faces a battle for the fate of the world, ultimately awakening their true powers and restoring peace, though a new threat emerges quietly in the shadows. The series centers on Immortals whose supernatural gifts let them fight evil and protect those in need, combining suspense with fantasy and gentle humor.
	

	The cast is led by emerging actor Zhang Wan Ying (“Glory”) as He Haining, Leo Zhou (“Relying on Favors”) as Dong Fang Shuo and Nick Shan (“Creation of The Gods I: Kingdom of Storms”) as Lu Xian.


	Yu Ji, a noted director of internet midform series, directed “VIII: Awakening.” KC Global Media Asia partners Andy Kaplan and George Chien executive produced. Meng Xun, who has worked with directors including John Woo and Wong Kar-Wai, served as production designer.

	“KC Global Media Asia is looking forward to being a part of bringing such an exciting project to global audiences,” said Bonnie Wiryani, VP and head of content sales. “Viewers are more and more interested in seeing local and cultural stories developed creatively and ‘VIII: Awakening’ has all the artistry, action, mystery, fantasy and folklore that we believe will resonate widely. There is great potential for the story to grow beyond a single title and develop into a broader universe in the future.”
	

	The production is a partnership between CICC (China Intercontinental Communication Center) and Shanghai Qi’Ai Film & TV Culture Co., Ltd. This marks the first original production in China for KC Global Media Asia, which will also handle its international sales. The deal reinforces the company’s continued efforts to grow its distribution business, build creative production partnerships and deliver a broader range of high-quality stories with international appeal.

	KC Global Media Entertainment LLC is headquartered in the U.S. with offices in Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, China, the Philippines and South Korea. Founded by former Sony executives Kaplan and Chien, KC Global Media Asia’s portfolio includes AXN, Animax, ONE, KCM and AXN Sports.

title: Andrew Garfield Renews Calls for a Gay Spider-Man, 13 Years After Asking ‘Why Can’t He Be Into Boys?’
description: Andrew Garfield is reflecting on his viral interview from 2013 in which he questioned why there had not yet been a gay Spider-Man. The Oscar nominee
body:
Andrew Garfield is reflecting on his viral interview from 2013 in which he questioned why there had not yet been a gay Spider-Man. The Oscar nominee was promoting “The Amazing Spider-Man 2” at the time when he told Entertainment Weekly about a recent discussion he had with producer Matt Tolmach about gender-swapping Peter Parker’s iconic love interest Mary-Jane, since she’s also just known as MJ.

	“I was kind of joking, but kind of not joking about MJ… I was like, ‘What if MJ is a dude?’” Garfield said in 2013. “Why can’t we discover that Peter is exploring his sexuality? It’s hardly even groundbreaking! … So why can’t he be gay? Why can’t he be into boys?”
	

	Garfield even pitched having Michael J. Bordan join his “Amazing Spider-Man” franchise as a male MJ, adding: “I’ve been obsessed with him since ‘The Wire.’ He’s so charismatic and talented. It’d be even better — we’d have interracial bisexuality!”

	Now on his 2026 press tour for Paul Greengrass’ “The Uprising,” Garfield was asked by EW to reflect on his 13-year-old call for a gay Spider-Man.

	“It was an exercise in rebellion that I felt passionate about,” Garfield said. “I just still believe that anyone can be in that suit. That’s the point of why it’s such a kind of universally beloved character, one of the greatly beloved characters in the history of fiction is because you don’t see skin color, you don’t see gender, you don’t see sexuality. Anyone can project themselves into that suit.”  

	Garfield continued, “I like the idea of a place where everyone is being honored and everyone is being included, and it was just a kind of act of saying, ‘Well, why not?’ And you’ll be telling on yourself if you have a strong opinion either way.”
	

	Tom Holland currently holds the title of Spider-Man on the big screen, with his latest outing, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” breaking box office records this summer to become one of the top grossers in film history. The actor has already expressed interest in diversifying the role with the addition of a live-action Miles Morales. Holland told the AP on the “Brand New Day” press tour that he has a “desire to bring Miles to the screen” and to “shepherd the lucky young kid who gets that job.”

schema.headline: Andrew Garfield Renews Calls for a Gay Spider-Man, 13 Years After Asking ‘Why Can’t He Be Into Boys?’

title: Tony Romo Suggests He’d Like to Return to CBS’ NFL Coverage After No Contest Plea
description: Tony Romo has analyzed plays for CBS Sports since 2017. Now he’s considering a new one, in which he hopes the network allows him to return following
body:
Tony Romo has analyzed plays for CBS Sports since 2017. Now he’s considering a new one, in which he hopes the network allows him to return following a run-in with the law.

	Romo on Tuesday said he pleaded no contest to a charge of operating while intoxicated stemming from an incident that took place in Milwaukee in July, and expressed hope in a statement that he’d be able to resume his NFL duties for the Paramount Skydance broadcast network. CBS Sports placed the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback on leave after he was arrested following a traffic stop made on Interstate 43 in Wisconsin.  
	

	CBS has not commented on the situation since sports chief David Berson said last month that the company had no timeline for Romo’s return, and wanted to put its focus on promoting its NFL slate. CBS Sports has tapped JJ Watt to pick up duties alongside regulars Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson when the network’s first Sunday football telecast takes place September 13.


	“The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant,” Romo said via a statement released on social media “It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully — to the Lord, to myself, to my family and now to the public.”

	He cited multiple back surgeries that spurred his retirement from the NFL as a factor in the incident, noting they “left me with constant, debilitating pain” which  “led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol.”

	“None of this is an excuse,” Romo said. “These are my failures and I take responsibility for them.”
	

	Romo, whose deal with CBS was valued in 2020 at about $17 million per year, has been an instrumental part of the company’s roster of sports talent, and the company’s decision to put him on leave could have consequences beyond who will call the opening game in CBS’ next season of telecasting professional football in the afternoon. The NFL has already held preliminary talks with CBS parent Paramount Skydance, according to two people familiar with the matter, about certain terms of a new rights deal. The change of control of the company, which is backed by the Ellison family, who bought Paramount from longtime owner Shari Redstone, triggered the league’s ability to discuss terms.

	CBS, like Fox, NBCUniversal, Disney and Amazon, is in the middle of an 11-year pact with the NFL that will keep games tied to those companies through 2033. The challenge? The league has an option that allows it to renegotiate terms with most of the companies after 2029, and with Disney after 2030.

	Romo only had experience on the field when he joined CBS Sports in 2017 as the lead game analyst on the network’s popular “NFL on CBS.” Behind the scenes, however, Romo worked with CBS football producer Jim Rikhoff to find his footing in the studio. “We rehearsed different games, old games, took the audio off, did a lot of trial and error, until we found his voice,” Rikhoff told Variety in 2019. “He’s experienced and talks about the games in ways that most people understand,” he said. “It really feels authentic. I try to stay out of his way and give him as much leeway as I can.”

	Romo’s acumen for predicting game play drew notice almost immediately, and lent new polish to a broadcast that has been around since the days of Brent Musburger and Pat Summerall.

	Romo said he has enlisted  doctors to help him “make the necessary changes” for his well-being. “As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period,” Romo added. Given the importance of NFL games to the business of CBS and the popularity of the game among American audiences, it’s not clear he’ll get it.

schema.headline: Tony Romo Suggests He’d Like to Return to CBS’ NFL Coverage After No Contest Plea

title: Variety and Utopai Studios to Host Future in Focus Conversations at TIFF
description: Variety Future in Focus, presented by Utopai Studios, will bring together leading filmmakers and creative voices at the Toronto International Film F
body:
Variety Future in Focus, presented by Utopai Studios, will bring together leading filmmakers and creative voices at the Toronto International Film Festival. The invite-only event, presented on Sept. 12, will explore how innovation is shaping the art and craft of filmmaking.

	James McAvoy will join Variety for a conversation about his work and perspective on the evolving art of storytelling, including his work directing and producing “California Schemin.’” He also stars in the film “Faith,” premiering at TIFF.
	

	The Future in Focus event will also feature an intimate conversation with Rachel Morrison, Academy Award-nominated cinematographer and director of “Love of Your Life,” also premiering at TIFF. Moderated by Variety senior entertainment writer Angelique Jackson, the conversation will explore Morrison’s creative process and approach to filmmaking.


	In other highlights, Stephanie Ahn, writer and director of “Bedford Park”; Carsten Kurpanek, Head of Production at Utopai Studios and editor of “Coyote vs. Acme”; Liz Garbus, Director of “Give Me the Ball!” and Co-founder, Story Syndicate; Rebel Wilson, director, writer and actor of “Girl Group”; and Basil Iwanyk, producer and founder and CEO, Thunder Road Films will participate in a panel discussion looking at innovation in filmmaking, spanning the latest trends in AI, immersive storytelling and more. During the panel moderated by Matt Donnelly, Variety Executive Editor, Film, panelists will share how they are building compelling worlds and characters in film now.

	“At Utopai Studios, we are building a new model for filmmaking that gives artists more ways to bring ambitious ideas to the screen while keeping their creative vision at the center of every production,” said Kevin Chong, COO of Utopai Studios. “The future of film will be shaped by the convergence of artistry, technology and new production methods, which is why we’re thrilled to partner with Variety at TIFF. We look forward to exploring how new tools, techniques and creative approaches are expanding what filmmakers can achieve and how their stories connect with audiences.”
	

	Together, these influential voices will offer a firsthand look at the creative ideas, technologies and techniques shaping the future of filmmaking and the talent leading the way.

schema.headline: Variety and Utopai Studios to Host Future in Focus Conversations at TIFF

title: Producer Urged Trump to Back U.S. Film Incentive Citing Prospect of Shooting Richard Nixon Biopic Overseas
description: President Donald Trump came away from a meeting with actor Jon Voight and two Hollywood producers very supportive of a federal tax incentive for fil
body:
President Donald Trump came away from a meeting with actor Jon Voight and two Hollywood producers very supportive of a federal tax incentive for film and TV productions. Something that may have caught Trump’s attention was the explanation by one of the producers that he would be forced to shoot a planned biopic of Richard Nixon outside of the U.S. unless there was an American tax incentive.

	At Monday’s meeting at the White House with Trump, actor Jon Voight — who is Trump’s “special ambassador” to Hollywood — was joined by SP Media Group chairman and CEO Steven Paul and president Scott Karol. The meeting marked the latest step in an initiative that began when President Trump asked Voight, Paul and Karol to assess the challenges facing the U.S. entertainment industry and recommend measures to restore domestic production.
	

	During the Aug. 31 meeting, Voight, Paul and Karol told the president that the industry had reached a critical point, with thousands of workers already losing jobs as producers are increasingly turning to Canada, the U.K., Australia and other markets offering competitive incentives.

	Indeed, Paul cited his upcoming film about Nixon’s early years — which he said would need to be produced overseas without a viable U.S. tax incentive.

	“President Trump’s public support is a major step forward for American film and television production,” Paul said in a statement. “This is about rebuilding an industry that creates high-paying jobs across the country and ensuring that American stories are made by American workers here at home. We look forward to working with leaders in both parties to turn this momentum into legislation.”
	

	Karol told Trump that a federal incentive could revitalize the industry, return vital economic activity to the U.S. and support local communities nationwide, citing a forthcoming economic impact report prepared by the Motion Picture Association and the coalition. 

	“The president’s call for immediate, bipartisan action reflects the urgency facing American production,” Karol said. “A competitive federal incentive can help put crews back to work, keep investment in U.S. communities and create lasting economic benefits across the country.”

	Voight, for his part, read an “impassioned letter” urging the president to respond to the industry’s growing workforce and production crisis, according to the group.

	The group helped form a broad coalition supporting the initiative, following extensive discussions with entertainment unions, guilds, studio and streaming executives, producers, writers, directors, actors, talent agencies, state film commissioners and other industry leaders. The coalition includes the Motion Picture Association (MPA), SAG-AFTRA, Teamsters, the Writers Guild of America East and West, the Directors Guild of America, the Independent Film & Television Alliance, Producers United, IATSE, the Coalition of American Producers, Film USA and the Producers Guild of America. 

	As part of the effort, Voight, Paul and Karol also met with MPA Chairman and CEO Charlie Rivkin and SVPs of federal government affairs Josh Rogin and Hap Rigby.

	The MPA has been working with Voight to push for a 20% tax credit for U.S.-based productions.

	The group first presented its recommendations to President Trump at Mar-a-Lago, identifying a federal film and television production incentive as its leading priority. After Trump initially raised the prospect of tariffs on films made outside of the U.S. as a possible solution, Voight, Paul and Karol continued working with the coalition, White House advisers and members of Congress to focus the proposal on a federal incentive. A subsequent White House meeting in May further advanced the approach as the group detailed production slowdowns across the country, including in Georgia.

	Following Monday’s meeting, Trump posted on Truth Social: “Congress should approve, immediately, a Federal Production Incentive to create Entertainment Jobs in America,” calling on Republicans and Democrats to work together and immediately craft legislation. 
	

	In a follow-up post Tuesday, Trump wrote: “Great bipartisan response and support in Congress for the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. We will bring this once great industry BACK TO AMERICA. Thank you for your attention to this matter!”

	Paul is an independent film producer and chairman and CEO of SP Media Group, based on the Paramount Pictures lot in Hollywood. SPMG maintains a co-financing agreement with Paramount Pictures to co-produce feature films and has financed and produced over 30 motion pictures in the past five years.

	Pictured above (l. to r.): Jon Voight, Steven Paul, Donald Trump and Scott Karol in the Oval Office in May 2026

schema.headline: Producer Urged Trump to Back U.S. Film Incentive Citing Prospect of Shooting Richard Nixon Biopic Overseas

title: ‘Avengers: Secret Wars’ Adds Noah Jupe to Cast
description: Noah Jupe will be the latest actor to join the Marvel Cinematic Universe, with the “Hamnet” and “A Quiet Place” star tapped to play a top-secret rol
body:
Noah Jupe will be the latest actor to join the Marvel Cinematic Universe, with the “Hamnet” and “A Quiet Place” star tapped to play a top-secret role in “Avengers: Secret Wars.”

	The superhero team-up movie, directed by Anthony and Joe Russo and produced by Marvel chief Kevin Feige, is the follow-up to “Avengers: Doomsday.” That movie doesn’t debut until Dec. 18, but production on “Secret Wars” is set to begin later this year (ahead of a Dec. 17, 2027 release date), kicking casting rumors into high gear.
	

	Marvel had no comment on Jupe’s casting.


	As a child actor, Jupe garnered attention for his standout turns in the TV series “The Night Manager” and “The Undoing,” before breaking out on the big screen with “Honey Boy” (for which he earned an Independent Spirit Award nomination) and the “Quiet Place” movies. The British actor recently appeared in Chloe Zhao’s Oscar-winning film “Hamnet” alongside Paul Mescal, Jessie Buckley and his younger brother, Jacobi Jupe.

	“Secret Wars” will likely reunite Jupe with his most recent co-star, Sadie Sink, who played the Juliet to his Romeo in a production of Shakespeare’s classic on London’s West End. Sink made her MCU debut as the mutant Jean Grey in July’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and will reprise her role in the forthcoming “X-Men” movie from Jake Schreier.

	“Doomsday” follows as Marvel superheroes from three distinct universes — namely the Avengers, the Fantastic Four and several of Fox’s O.G. X-Men — are set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever encountered: Victor Von Doom.
	

	Marvel’s new Big Bad is played by Robert Downey Jr., whose original “Avengers” character Tony Stark/Iron Man died in 2019’s “Endgame.” The film features a sprawling cast of A-listers, including Chris Evans (returning as Steve Rogers), Chris Hemsworth, Pedro Pascal, Paul Rudd, Anthony Mackie, Florence Pugh, Vanessa Kirby, Channing Tatum, Simu Liu, Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen and Tom Hiddleston. 

	Not much has been revealed about “Secret Wars,” which is said to be even larger in scale than “Doomsday,” leading audiences to believe that more superheroes (like Tom Holland’s Spider-Man or Benedict Cumberbatch’s Doctor Strange) will return. If the movie follows the comic run of the same name, it could bring together every hero from across the MCU multiverse into one dimension called Battleworld. In the comics, Battleworld stitched together all the different worlds and plopped every hero and their variants into a new universe.

	Deadline first reported Jupe’s casting. He is repped by WME and Brillstein Entertainment Partners.

schema.headline: ‘Avengers: Secret Wars’ Adds Noah Jupe to Cast

            Alanis Morissette claims she is the victim of a “calculated blackmail campaign” orchestrated by her former tour manager ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, Alanis is suing a woman named Keren Urinov for civil extortion, fraud, and negligent misrepresentation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Alanis claims that while temporarily employed by her as a tour manager, Keren admitted to the British Border Force that a bag seized at an airport on July 12, 2025 -- which allegedly contained marijuana and a non-opioid animal tranquilizer called zylazine -- belonged to her.

            In the docs, Alanis insists she will not be bullied into giving her blackmailer a huge payday and is now suing her over it.

            The Bunny Ranch empire built by late brothel owner Dennis Hof is officially up for grabs ... with the Nevada business hitting the market for $33.9 million ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to an offering memorandum obtained by TMZ ... the Bunny Ranch portfolio is being sold as one package. It includes the Moonlite Bunny Ranch, Sagebrush Ranch and Love Ranch, plus 11 Nevada real estate parcels.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The sale also includes four licensed businesses, residential properties, support buildings, storage facilities, development land, highway frontage, vehicles, equipment, trade names, websites, and other digital assets.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The properties are located in Northern Nevada near Reno, Carson City, and the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center. The flagship Moonlite property spans 20 acres, while Sagebrush Ranch sits on 15 acres and Love Ranch covers nearly 2 acres.
      
    
            Hof famously turned his legal brothels into a media empire, with Moonlite featured on HBO's "Cathouse: The Series." He also ran for political office in 2018, winning a Nevada State Assembly seat posthumously after dying at age 72.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Hof was found dead at his Love Ranch home in Nevada in October 2018 ... with porn star Ron Jeremy discovering his body after friends became concerned when Hof stopped answering his phone.
      
    
            Lamar Odom's near-fatal 2015 drug overdose occurred at Love Ranch South, a separate legal brothel branch in Nevada that was owned by Hof and was previously sold.

            Jared Leto has quietly offloaded his massive L.A. mansion -- a former Air Force compound -- and the timing of the sale might raise some eyebrows.
      
    
            We've learned the actor and singer sold his 14,649-square-foot mansion in May for $12 million ... a tidy profit after buying the pad for $5 million back in 2015.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The 6-bedroom, 5-bathroom home -- which sits on a 1.4-acre lot -- has a colorful history ... having previously been a U.S. Air Force installation with connections to the country's atomic bomb program.
      
    
            Army training films and Air Force newsreels were also shot at the property during the Cold War ... and the short reels even featured huge stars like Bob Hope, Jimmy Stewart, James Garner, Kim Novak and Gregory Peck.
      
    
            The main structure has 3 35-millimeter screening rooms and temperature-controlled film vaults. It also has a full sound stage.
      
    
            Leto's decision to let the place go comes during a particularly turbulent time in the star's life ... with the house selling just two months before the BBC released its documentary in which multiple women accused Leto of sexual assault. Several allegations against him first cropped up in British newspapers last year.
      
    
            While he's vigorously denied all wrongdoing, he's receded from the spotlight in recent months ... and making the quiet decision to leave Los Angeles seems to indicate he's done with Hollywood in the long term.
